mainEntity.name: Is it normal for a new veneer to feel raised immediately after placement?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be relatively common to notice a slightly unfamiliar sensation in the days immediately following veneer placement. Some patients experience a brief adaptation period as the tongue and jaw adjust to the new restoration. However, if the raised sensation is significant or does not resolve within a few days, it is advisable to contact your dental practice. A straightforward bite check and any necessary adjustment can usually be carried out promptly and comfortably.

mainEntity.name: Can a raised veneer cause long-term damage if left untreated?

acceptedAnswer.text: If a veneer consistently sits higher than surrounding teeth, it may over time contribute to uneven bite pressure. This can affect the veneered tooth, adjacent teeth, and potentially the jaw joint. In most cases, the issue is minor and easily corrected. However, prolonged bite imbalance is worth addressing sooner rather than later to minimise any cumulative effects. Your dental professional can assess the extent of the issue during a clinical examination and recommend appropriate management.

mainEntity.name: Could my veneer be coming loose if it feels raised?

acceptedAnswer.text: A raised sensation does not automatically mean your veneer is coming loose. However, partial debonding — where the veneer begins to lift at its edges — is one possible cause. Signs that may suggest debonding include a sensation that the veneer moves slightly, a change in its appearance, or discomfort. If you suspect debonding, arrange a dental appointment at your earliest convenience to have the veneer assessed and, if necessary, re-bonded or replaced.

mainEntity.name: How long does a veneer adjustment appointment take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most veneer adjustment appointments are relatively brief. A bite assessment and minor occlusal adjustment can typically be completed within 20 to 30 minutes. The procedure generally requires no anaesthetic and is well tolerated by most patients. Your dentist will take the time necessary to ensure the bite feels balanced and comfortable before concluding the appointment.

mainEntity.name: Can teeth grinding cause a veneer to feel raised over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Bruxism — the habitual grinding or clenching of teeth — generates significant forces that can affect dental restorations, including veneers. Over time, grinding can alter the surface of a veneer, change how it interacts with opposing teeth, and potentially weaken the bond between the veneer and the natural tooth. If you are aware that you grind your teeth, discussing the use of a protective nightguard with your dentist is strongly advisable. This can help protect both your veneers and your natural dentition.

mainEntity.name: How often should patients with veneers attend dental check-ups?

acceptedAnswer.text: Patients with veneers are generally advised to attend dental check-ups at the same frequency as all patients — typically every six to twelve months, depending on individual clinical needs. During these appointments, your dentist will examine the condition of your veneers, assess your overall oral health, and identify any changes that may require attention. Regular professional cleaning appointments with a dental hygienist are also beneficial for maintaining the health of the gum tissue surrounding your restorations.
